1	/**
2	 * Data-use terms: the contract a session's transcript is held under, pinned to
3	 * the session log at creation so every later reader — an export, a curator, a
4	 * client auditor — learns from the log alone what the transcript may serve.
5	 * A pin may narrow the terms and never widen their purposes, so a session
6	 * created for delivery cannot become training data after the fact. Nothing here
7	 * reaches a model request. The
8	 * [attributable-decisions Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md)
9	 * owns the design rationale.
10	 * @module @deepseek-ai/dsh-data-use
11	 */
12	
13	import { Context, Service } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'
14	import z from '@deepseek-ai/schemastery'
15	import type { Agent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
16	// Type-only: resolves the `agent/session-start` event this service pins on.
17	import type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
18	import { HarnessError } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
19	import type { SessionEvent } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
20	import type { DataUsePurpose, DataUseTerms } from './types.ts'
21	
22	export type * from './types.ts'
23	
24	declare module '@deepseek-ai/cordis' {
25	  interface Context {
26	    dataUse: DataUseService
27	  }
28	}
29	
30	/** Every {@link DataUsePurpose}, for validation and for option advertisement. */
31	export const DATA_USE_PURPOSES: readonly DataUsePurpose[] = ['delivery', 'training', 'evaluation']
32	
33	/** Stable error codes of terms this service refuses. */
34	export type DataUseErrorCode = 'DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG' | 'DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS' | 'DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED'
35	
36	/** Error returned when configured or pinned terms cannot hold a session. */
37	export class DataUseError extends HarnessError {
38	  /**
39	   * @param message - human-readable reason, naming the field at fault.
40	   * @param code - stable machine-routable classification.
41	   */
42	  // Keep the constructor to narrow HarnessError's string code at this boundary.
43	  // oxlint-disable-next-line typescript/no-useless-constructor -- type-only narrowing
44	  constructor(message: string, code: DataUseErrorCode) {
45	    super(message, code)
46	  }
47	}
48	
49	/** The deployment's default terms, validated from `cordis.yml`. */
50	export interface Config {
51	  /** The client every session of this deployment belongs to. */
52	  clientId: string
53	  /** The agreement the terms come from. */
54	  agreementId: string
55	  /** Non-empty subset of {@link DATA_USE_PURPOSES}, each named once. */
56	  purposes: DataUsePurpose[]
57	  /** Region the transcripts may live in. */
58	  residency: string
59	  /** Positive number of days a transcript is kept. */
60	  retentionDays: number
61	  /** Versioned redaction profile an export applies. */
62	  redactionProfile: string
63	}
64	
65	/**
66	 * The terms currently pinned to a log, or `undefined` when it carries none.
67	 * The pure fold — a consumer holding persisted events needs no service, and a
68	 * resumed session needs no catch-up because replaying the log IS the state.
69	 * @param events - session events in log order; other event types are skipped.
70	 * @returns the newest pinned terms, or `undefined` without any.
71	 */
72	export function termsOf(events: readonly SessionEvent[]): DataUseTerms | undefined {
73	  for (let index = events.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
74	    const event = events[index] as SessionEvent
75	    if (event.type === 'dataUse/terms') return event.data
76	  }
77	  return undefined
78	}
79	
80	/**
81	 * Whether `candidate` admits a purpose `standing` does not, which is the one
82	 * change a pin may never make.
83	 * @param standing - the terms the log already carries.
84	 * @param candidate - the terms a pin proposes.
85	 * @returns the purposes the candidate adds, empty when it only narrows.
86	 */
87	export function widenedPurposes(
88	  standing: DataUseTerms,
89	  candidate: DataUseTerms,
90	): readonly DataUsePurpose[] {
91	  return candidate.purposes.filter(purpose => !standing.purposes.includes(purpose))
92	}
93	
94	/** Data use (`ctx.dataUse`): the contract terms every session log states about itself. */
95	export class DataUseService extends Service {
96	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
97	    clientId: z.string().required(),
98	    agreementId: z.string().required(),
99	    purposes: z.array(z.union(['delivery', 'training', 'evaluation'] as const)).required(),
100	    residency: z.string().required(),
101	    retentionDays: z.natural().min(1).required(),
102	    redactionProfile: z.string().required(),
103	  })
104	
105	  private readonly defaults: DataUseTerms
106	
107	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config) {
108	    super(ctx, 'dataUse')
109	    this.defaults = validateTerms(
110	      {
111	        clientId: config.clientId,
112	        agreementId: config.agreementId,
113	        purposes: config.purposes,
114	        residency: config.residency,
115	        retentionDays: config.retentionDays,
116	        redactionProfile: config.redactionProfile,
117	      },
118	      'DATA_USE_INVALID_CONFIG',
119	    )
120	    ctx.on('agent/session-start', ({ agent }) => {
121	      // A resumed session keeps the terms it was created under; only a session
122	      // that carries none is pinned, so the record states creation-time terms.
123	      if (termsOf(agent.session.events) === undefined) {
124	        agent.session.append('dataUse/terms', this.defaults)
125	      }
126	    })
127	  }
128	
129	  /** The deployment's configured default terms, as every fresh session is pinned with. */
130	  get defaultTerms(): DataUseTerms {
131	    return this.defaults
132	  }
133	
134	  /**
135	   * Pin narrower terms to one session and return the record as it was appended.
136	   * @param agent - the agent whose session the terms hold.
137	   * @param terms - the terms to record; their purposes may not exceed the session's.
138	   * @returns the terms exactly as they were appended.
139	   * @throws {@link DataUseError} when a field is unusable, or when the pin would
140	   *   admit a purpose the session's standing terms do not.
141	   */
142	  pin(agent: Agent, terms: DataUseTerms): DataUseTerms {
143	    const validated = validateTerms(terms, 'DATA_USE_INVALID_TERMS')
144	    const standing = termsOf(agent.session.events)
145	    if (standing !== undefined) {
146	      const widened = widenedPurposes(standing, validated)
147	      if (widened.length > 0) {
148	        throw new DataUseError(
149	          `this session is pinned to purposes ${standing.purposes.join(', ')}, which the pin widens with ${widened.join(', ')}`,
150	          'DATA_USE_TERMS_PINNED',
151	        )
152	      }
153	    }
154	    agent.session.append('dataUse/terms', validated)
155	    return validated
156	  }
157	}
158	
159	/**
160	 * Reject every field a durable record may not carry, then freeze the record.
161	 * @param terms - the candidate terms, from configuration or from a pin.
162	 * @param code - the classification a rejection carries.
163	 * @returns the terms as a detached record.
164	 */
165	function validateTerms(terms: DataUseTerms, code: DataUseErrorCode): DataUseTerms {
166	  for (const [field, value] of [
167	    ['clientId', terms.clientId],
168	    ['agreementId', terms.agreementId],
169	    ['residency', terms.residency],
170	    ['redactionProfile', terms.redactionProfile],
171	  ] as const) {
172	    if (value.length === 0) throw new DataUseError(`${field} is empty, so the terms state no ${field}`, code)
173	  }
174	  if (terms.purposes.length === 0) throw new DataUseError('purposes is empty, so the terms admit nothing at all', code)
175	  const seen = new Set<DataUsePurpose>()
176	  for (const purpose of terms.purposes) {
177	    if (!DATA_USE_PURPOSES.includes(purpose)) {
178	      throw new DataUseError(`purpose ${JSON.stringify(purpose)} is not one of ${DATA_USE_PURPOSES.join(', ')}`, code)
179	    }
180	    if (seen.has(purpose)) throw new DataUseError(`purpose ${JSON.stringify(purpose)} is listed twice`, code)
181	    seen.add(purpose)
182	  }
183	  if (!Number.isInteger(terms.retentionDays) || terms.retentionDays < 1) {
184	    throw new DataUseError(`retentionDays ${String(terms.retentionDays)} is not a positive whole number of days`, code)
185	  }
186	  return {
187	    clientId: terms.clientId,
188	    agreementId: terms.agreementId,
189	    purposes: [...terms.purposes],
190	    residency: terms.residency,
191	    retentionDays: terms.retentionDays,
192	    redactionProfile: terms.redactionProfile,
193	  }
194	}
195	
196	export default DataUseService

118	    const profile = this.resolveProfile(request.profile)
119	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
120	    const admitted = new Map<SessionId, DataUseTerms>()
121	    let withheldByTerms = 0
122	    const candidates = request.sessions ?? (await this.ctx.sessionPersistence.list()).map(header => header.id)

143	      sessions: [...admitted.keys()],

167	      ruleHits: Object.fromEntries(profile.rules.map(rule => [rule.id, ruleHits.get(rule.id) ?? 0])),

190	   */
191	  private resolveProfile(requested: string | undefined): RedactionProfile {
192	    const id = requested ?? this.defaultProfile
193	    if (id === undefined) {
194	      throw new CuratorError(
195	        'this export names no redaction profile and no defaultProfile is configured; a curated export never runs unredacted',
196	        'CURATOR_PROFILE_REQUIRED',
197	      )
198	    }
199	    const profile = this.profiles.get(id)
200	    if (profile === undefined) {
201	      throw new CuratorError(
202	        `redaction profile "${id}" is not configured; this deployment configured ${[...this.profiles.keys()].join(', ')}`,
203	        'CURATOR_PROFILE_UNKNOWN',
204	      )
205	    }
206	    return profile

209	  /**

211	   * @param record - the record the exporter serialized.
212	   * @param profile - the profile this export runs under.
213	   * @param admitted - the terms of every session the terms pass admitted.
214	   * @param ruleHits - export-wide replacement counts, incremented in place.
215	   * @returns the curated line, newline included.
216	   * @throws {@link CuratorError} when the record names a session the terms pass did not admit.
217	   */
218	  private curate(
219	    record: Trajectory,
220	    profile: RedactionProfile,
221	    admitted: ReadonlyMap<SessionId, DataUseTerms>,
222	    ruleHits: Map<string, number>,
223	  ): string {
224	    const terms = admitted.get(record.id)
225	    /* v8 ignore next 4 -- the exporter reads only the sessions the terms pass admitted and mapped. */
226	    if (terms === undefined) {
227	      throw new CuratorError(
228	        `session ${record.id} reached the sink without admitted terms`,
229	        'CURATOR_UNADMITTED_RECORD',
230	      )
231	    }
232	    const hits = new Map<string, number>()
233	    const redacted = redactTrajectory(record, profile.rules, hits)
234	    for (const [id, count] of hits) ruleHits.set(id, (ruleHits.get(id) ?? 0) + count)

236	      ...redacted,
237	      curation: {
238	        redactionApplied: true,
239	        redaction: { profile: profile.id, profileSha256: profile.sha256, hits: Object.fromEntries(hits) },
240	        residency: terms.residency,
241	      },

244	  }

79	/** Trajectory exporter (`ctx.trajectories`): persisted sessions as training and evaluation records. */
80	export class TrajectoryService extends Service {
81	  static inject = ['sessionPersistence']
82	
83	  static Config: z<Config> = z.object({
84	    withheldDistricts: z.array(z.string()).default([]),
85	  })
86	
87	  private readonly resolved: ResolvedConfig
88	
89	  constructor(ctx: Context, config: Config = {}) {
90	    super(ctx, 'trajectories')
91	    this.resolved = resolveConfig(config)
92	  }
93	
94	  /**
95	   * Fold the requested sessions and write one line per trajectory. A session
96	   * that cannot be read or folded is reported and the export continues; the
97	   * sink is closed exactly once when every session has been handled.
98	   * @param request - sessions to export, the destination sink, the reward filter, the held-out opt-in, and the districts to write.
99	   * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, rewarded lines, filtered
100	   *   sessions, withheld held-out and district sessions, and skips with reasons.
101	   */
102	  async export(request: TrajectoryExportRequest): Promise<TrajectoryExportReport> {
103	    const persistence = this.ctx.sessionPersistence
104	    const sessions = request.sessions ?? (await persistence.list()).map(header => header.id)
105	    const skipped: TrajectoryExportSkip[] = []
106	    let exported = 0
107	    let rewarded = 0
108	    let filtered = 0
109	    let heldOut = 0
110	    let withheld = 0
111	    try {
112	      for (const sessionId of sessions) {
113	        let line: string
114	        let outcome: 1 | 0 | null
115	        let reserved: boolean
116	        let district: string | undefined
117	        try {
118	          const { meta, events } = await persistence.inspect(sessionId)
119	          const trajectory = foldTrajectory(meta, events)
120	          outcome = trajectory.reward.outcome
121	          reserved = trajectory.environment?.heldOut === true
122	          district = trajectory.environment?.district
123	          line = `${JSON.stringify(trajectory)}\n`
124	        } catch (error: unknown) {
125	          skipped.push({ sessionId, reason: reasonOf(error) })
126	          continue
127	        }
128	        if (reserved && request.includeHeldOut !== true) {
129	          heldOut += 1
130	          continue
131	        }
132	        if (this.withholds(district, request.districts)) {
133	          withheld += 1
134	          continue
135	        }
136	        if (request.rewardedOnly === true && outcome !== 1) {
137	          filtered += 1
138	          continue
139	        }
140	        await request.sink.write(line)
141	        exported += 1
142	        if (outcome === 1) rewarded += 1
143	      }
144	    } finally {
145	      await request.sink.close()
146	    }
147	    return { sessions: sessions.length, exported, rewarded, filtered, heldOut, withheld, skipped }
148	  }

150	  /**
151	   * Whether a session's district keeps it out of this export: a request that
152	   * names districts writes exactly those, and one that names none withholds
153	   * the configured districts.
154	   */
155	  private withholds(district: string | undefined, districts: readonly string[] | undefined): boolean {
156	    if (districts !== undefined) return district === undefined || !districts.includes(district)
157	    return district !== undefined && this.resolved.withheldDistricts.includes(district)
158	  }
159	}

1	# @deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories
2	
3	English | [中文](README.zh.md)
4	
5	Trajectory export: persisted sessions folded into `dsh-trajectory/1` records, one JSON line each, with the chat-format message list a trainer's template consumes, the reward a certificate decided, and the components that were in play. Export reads through the session persistence seam and writes no session event. The [trajectory-export Agent Note](../../../.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-trajectory-export-and-environment-registry.md) owns the design rationale.
6	
7	## Config
8	
9	```yaml
10	- id: persistence
11	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl'
12	  config:
13	    root: './.sessions'
14	- id: trajectories
15	  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-trajectories'
16	  config:
17	    withheldDistricts:
18	      - workshop
19	```
20	
21	| Field | Meaning |
22	|---|---|
23	| `withheldDistricts` (default `[]`) | Districts an export that names none withholds, counted as `withheld`. The package ships no district name: a deployment states which of its districts may not leave by default, the way a client-facing district does. |
24	
25	The service requires a session persistence backend. `resolveConfig(config)` is the exported defaulting step.
26	
27	## Service contract
28	
29	`ctx.trajectories.export({ sessions?, sink, rewardedOnly?, includeHeldOut?, districts? })` folds each named session (or every persisted session when `sessions` is absent) through `ctx.sessionPersistence.inspect()` and writes `JSON.stringify(trajectory) + '\n'` to `sink.write()`; a session that cannot be read or folded is added to `skipped` with its reason and the export continues.
30	
31	Three filters run in order over each readable session. A session whose `environment/run` stamp marks a held-out environment is withheld and counted as `heldOut` unless `includeHeldOut: true`, so evaluation tasks never become training data by default. Then the district decides: with `districts` named, only a session whose stamp carries one of them is written, which is how an export reaches a district the deployment otherwise withholds; with no `districts` named, a session whose stamp carries a configured `withheldDistricts` entry is withheld. Either way the withheld sessions are counted as `withheld`. Last, `rewardedOnly: true` withholds trajectories whose reward outcome is not `1` and counts them as `filtered`.
32	
33	The sink is closed exactly once, after the last write or after a failure. The report carries `sessions`, `exported`, `rewarded`, `filtered`, `heldOut`, `withheld`, and `skipped`. `jsonlFileSink(path)` is the shipped file sink; it truncates the file on first use.
34	
35	`foldTrajectory(meta, events)` is the pure projection behind the service and is exported for tests and offline tools. It is deterministic for the same inputs.
36	
37	`foldTrajectoryReward(events)` decides the reward from the log's goal and verification events. A session whose last recorded [`verification/run`](../../verification/verification/README.md#what-a-runs-verdict-says) carries `verdict: 'tampered'` scores `outcome: 0` on the `tamper` basis whatever else the log holds, because a run that found the files it measures the task with changed says the measurement is void — a failed check means the work is incomplete, so folding the two would let a workspace whose checks no longer describe the task earn partial credit. Otherwise the verifier decides whenever a standard exists, an uncertified completion is undecided, and a log without a goal is unmeasured.
38	
39	`outcome` stays certificate-based, and `parity` is the auxiliary signal beside it. A run of [weighted cases](../../verification/verification/README.md#parity-and-what-it-does-not-decide) records its weighted pass rate on the `verification/run` event, and the record carries the last run's as its own `parity` field. It never replaces `outcome`: a pass rate is gameable by a candidate that overfits the failures it was shown and abandons the rest, so a session that passed most of a standard's case weight and one that passed none both export `outcome: 0` until a certificate covers the revision. A training run may shape a reward with `parity`; nothing may optimize it alone.
40	
41	## Record format `dsh-trajectory/1`
42	
43	| Field | Content |
44	|---|---|
45	| `id`, `source` | Session id; creation time, working directory, parent session, and the agent preset the log last selected |
46	| `environment` | The `environment/run` stamp the runner appended: environment id and kind, held-out flag, content hashes of prompt, fixture, and checks, repetition, group, and district, model route, declared isolation; absent for a session no runner stamped |
47	| `config`, `system`, `tools` | Call configuration, rendered system prompt, and tool schemas of the last `request/header` |
48	| `messages` | Surface messages in model-visible order after compaction replacements: `user`, `assistant` (with `toolCalls` when requested), and `tool` (with `toolCallId`, `isError`) roles; each carries the `seq` of its source event, its `turn` and `step`, its content blocks verbatim (reasoning included), and the recorded source kind |
49	| `steps` | One entry per model call with the adapter-reported usage |
50	| `reward` | `outcome` `1` when a certificate covers the current standard revision, `0` when a standard exists without one, `null` otherwise; `basis` `tamper` (the last recorded run found the check-owned files changed), `certificate`, `uncertified-completion` (goal completed, no standard ever authored), or `none` (no goal); the goal snapshot, the covering certificate, and the attempt, directive, and relaxation counts |
51	| `parity` | `{ weightPassed, weightTotal }` of the last recorded run, absent when that run measured no cases |
52	| `provenance` | Component ids in the component registry's scheme (`composition:<preset>`, `environment:<id>`, `model-provider:<provider>`, `tool:<name>`), tool names in first-use order, and the certificate's isolation level |
53	
54	Token ids and logprobs are absent: the harness never sees token ids, and on-policy capture belongs to a trainer's inference proxy.
55	
56	## Model Experience
57	
58	None, as export reads persisted logs and writes files; it adds nothing to any model request.
59	
60	#### KV Cache effect
61	
62	None; the service neither adds to nor changes any model request.
63	
64	## Known Limitations and Deferred Work
65	
66	- **Off-policy text** — a trainer re-tokenizes exported text through its chat template, which suits supervised and rejection-sampled training; strict on-policy reinforcement learning needs an inference proxy in front of the harness.
67	- **This service redacts nothing** — tool results may carry credentials or private data, and `export()` writes them as folded. [`@deepseek-ai/dsh-curator`](../../governance/curator/README.md) is the export path that applies a redaction profile and the session's data-use terms; a deployment calling this service directly gets the unredacted lines.
68	- **District withholding reads the stamp** — a session no runner stamped, or one stamped before its district was configured, carries no district and no configured withholding reaches it; an export that names districts writes only stamped sessions.
69	- **One standard per session** — the reward reads the session's verification fold, which holds one completion standard; a session measuring several goals is scored by the standard in force.
70	- **No rejection-sampling export** — lines carry the environment stamp, so a consumer can group by environment, repetition, and group, but the exporter does not yet select the best of N per environment or emit per-environment statistics.
71	- **Truncation scores as failure** — a session that stopped on a token limit, an abort, or a provider error under a measured goal exports with outcome `0`; the turn-end reason is not yet a field of the record, so a trainer cannot mask it.

3	// data/proving-ground/datasets/<name>/: train.jsonl, heldout.jsonl, and a
4	// manifest with the source records, the counts, the distributions of the
5	// written train set, the token totals, and every written file's SHA-256.
6	// Node built-ins only.

8	// Usage: node build-dataset.mjs <name> [--include-delegated] [--include-held-out] [--check]

17	// trajectories.jsonl. Held-out environments never reach train.jsonl, and
18	// without --include-held-out they reach no file at all, so a trainer pointed
19	// at the directory cannot take an evaluation task by accident.

50	  { name: 'anthropic-key', re: /sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}/g },
51	  { name: 'openai-style-key', re: /\bsk-(?:proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}/g },
52	  { name: 'github-token', re: /\b(?:ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr)_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}|\bgithub_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,}/g },
53	  { name: 'aws-access-key', re: /\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b/g },
54	  { name: 'slack-token', re: /\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}/g },
55	  { name: 'private-key', re: /-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----/g },
56	  { name: 'bearer-token', re: /\bBearer [A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]{20,}/g },
57	]
58	
59	/** An address with its mail domain captured, because the domain decides whether the match is a mailbox. */
60	const EMAIL_RE = /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+'-]+@([A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+)\b/g
61	/** Documentation and test domains RFC 2606 and RFC 6761 reserve: never a deliverable mailbox. */
62	const RESERVED_EMAIL_DOMAIN_RE = /(^|\.)(example\.(com|net|org|edu)|test|example|invalid|localhost)$/i
63	/**
64	 * Shortest registrable label this scan treats as a real mail domain. The
65	 * corpus's URI, query-string, and URL-template environments feed their parsers
66	 * stand-in addresses at one-to-three-letter domains (`x@y.com`, `foo@bar.com`,
67	 * `user@a.com`), while the providers an operator address could name are longer.
68	 * A real mailbox at a shorter domain (`qq.com`) passes the scan, so it bounds
69	 * the accident it was built for rather than every address that could exist.
70	 */
71	const MIN_MAILBOX_LABEL = 4
72	
73	/**
74	 * @param {Buffer | string} content bytes to digest
75	 * @returns {string} lowercase hex SHA-256
76	 */
77	function sha256(content) {
78	  return createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')
79	}
80	
81	/**
82	 * Parses the command line.
83	 * @param {string[]} argv arguments after the script path
84	 * @returns {{ name: string, includeDelegated: boolean, includeHeldOut: boolean, check: boolean }}
85	 */
86	function parseArgs(argv) {
87	  const options = { name: undefined, includeDelegated: false, includeHeldOut: false, check: false }
88	  for (const arg of argv) {
89	    if (arg === '--include-delegated') options.includeDelegated = true
90	    else if (arg === '--include-held-out') options.includeHeldOut = true
91	    else if (arg === '--check') options.check = true
92	    else if (arg.startsWith('--')) throw new Error(`unknown argument ${arg}`)
93	    else if (options.name === undefined) options.name = arg
94	    else throw new Error(`unexpected argument ${arg}`)
95	  }
96	  if (options.name === undefined) {
97	    throw new Error('usage: node build-dataset.mjs <name> [--include-delegated] [--include-held-out] [--check]')
98	  }
99	  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/.test(options.name)) throw new Error(`dataset name must be a plain directory name: ${options.name}`)
100	  return options
101	}
102	
103	/**
104	 * Reads the bench environment catalog: the tier and domain each `code:<task>` id was authored with.
105	 * @returns {Map<string, { tier: number, domain: string }>} keyed by environment id
106	 */
107	function readTaskCatalog() {
108	  if (!existsSync(TASKS_DIR)) throw new Error(`no environment catalog at ${relative(REPO_DIR, TASKS_DIR)}`)
109	  const catalog = new Map()
110	  for (const name of readdirSync(TASKS_DIR).sort()) {
111	    const path = join(TASKS_DIR, name, 'task.json')
112	    if (!existsSync(path)) continue
113	    const task = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path, 'utf8'))
114	    catalog.set(task.id, { tier: task.tier, domain: task.domain })
115	  }
116	  return catalog
117	}
118	
119	/**
120	 * The record directories that hold an export, in name order.
121	 * @returns {string[]} directory names under data/proving-ground/
122	 */
123	function recordNames() {
124	  return readdirSync(RUNS_DIR)
125	    .filter(name => !NON_RECORDS.has(name) && existsSync(join(RUNS_DIR, name, 'trajectories.jsonl')))
126	    .sort()
127	}
128	
129	/**
130	 * Yields every string the value holds, with the JSON path that reached it.
131	 * @param {unknown} value a parsed trajectory or any part of one
132	 * @param {string} path path of the value, for the report
133	 * @yields {{ path: string, text: string }} one string and where it sits
134	 */
135	function* strings(value, path) {
136	  if (typeof value === 'string') yield { path, text: value }
137	  else if (Array.isArray(value)) for (const [index, item] of value.entries()) yield* strings(item, `${path}[${index}]`)
138	  else if (value !== null && typeof value === 'object') for (const [key, item] of Object.entries(value)) yield* strings(item, `${path}.${key}`)
139	}
140	
141	/**
142	 * Whether one e-mail match names a mailbox rather than a parser fixture.
143	 * @param {string} domain the address's mail domain
144	 * @returns {boolean} true when the domain could receive mail
145	 */
146	function isMailboxDomain(domain) {
147	  if (RESERVED_EMAIL_DOMAIN_RE.test(domain)) return false
148	  const labels = domain.split('.')
149	  // A two-letter-or-shorter public suffix takes two labels (`x.co.uk`), so the registrable name sits one further left.
150	  const registrable = labels.length > 2 && labels.at(-2).length <= 3 ? labels.at(-3) : labels.at(-2)
151	  return registrable.length >= MIN_MAILBOX_LABEL
152	}
153	
154	/**
155	 * The matched text replaced by `[redacted]` inside a short window of its
156	 * string, so a refusal locates the hit without reprinting it.
157	 * @param {string} text the string the match was found in
158	 * @param {number} index where the match starts
159	 * @param {number} length how long the match is
160	 * @returns {string} a single-line excerpt
161	 */
162	function redactedExcerpt(text, index, length) {
163	  const window = 40
164	  const start = Math.max(0, index - window)
165	  const end = Math.min(text.length, index + length + window)
166	  const excerpt = `${start > 0 ? '…' : ''}${text.slice(start, index)}[redacted]${text.slice(index + length, end)}${end < text.length ? '…' : ''}`
167	  return excerpt.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
168	}
169	
170	/**
171	 * Scans one trajectory for credential- and mailbox-shaped strings.
172	 * @param {string} record the record directory the trajectory came from
173	 * @param {object} trajectory one parsed `dsh-trajectory/1` line
174	 * @param {object[]} hits collector every match is appended to
175	 */
176	function scanTrajectory(record, trajectory, hits) {
177	  const found = (path, pattern, text, match) => {
178	    hits.push({ record, id: trajectory.id, path, pattern, digest: sha256(match[0]), excerpt: redactedExcerpt(text, match.index, match[0].length) })
179	  }
180	  for (const { path, text } of strings(trajectory, 'trajectory')) {
181	    for (const { name, re } of SECRET_PATTERNS) {
182	      for (const match of text.matchAll(re)) found(path, name, text, match)
183	    }
184	    for (const match of text.matchAll(EMAIL_RE)) {
185	      if (isMailboxDomain(match[1])) found(path, 'email-address', text, match)
186	    }
187	  }
188	}
189	
190	/** Running token totals over the steps of the written trajectories. */
191	function newTokenTotals() {
192	  return { steps: 0, stepsWithUsage: 0, inputTokens: 0, outputTokens: 0 }
193	}
194	
195	/**
196	 * Adds one trajectory's steps to the running totals, keeping the optional
197	 * counters only when a step reported them.
198	 * @param {object} totals what {@link newTokenTotals} returned
199	 * @param {readonly object[]} steps the trajectory's steps
200	 */
201	function addUsage(totals, steps) {
202	  for (const step of steps) {
203	    totals.steps += 1
204	    if (step.usage === undefined) continue
205	    totals.stepsWithUsage += 1
206	    totals.inputTokens += step.usage.inputTokens ?? 0
207	    totals.outputTokens += step.usage.outputTokens ?? 0
208	    for (const key of ['cacheReadTokens', 'cacheWriteTokens', 'reasoningTokens']) {
209	      if (step.usage[key] !== undefined) totals[key] = (totals[key] ?? 0) + step.usage[key]
210	    }
211	  }
212	}
213	
214	/** The model route a stamp names, as `provider/model`. */
215	const routeOf = (model) => `${model.provider}/${model.model}`
216	
217	/**
218	 * Counts one key of one distribution.
219	 * @param {Map<string, Map<string, number>>} distributions every distribution by name
220	 * @param {string} name which distribution
221	 * @param {string} key the bucket
222	 */
223	function tally(distributions, name, key) {
224	  const bucket = distributions.get(name) ?? new Map()
225	  bucket.set(key, (bucket.get(key) ?? 0) + 1)
226	  distributions.set(name, bucket)
227	}
228	
229	/** Sorts a map's entries by key into a plain object, so the manifest reads the same on every build. */
230	function sorted(entries) {
231	  return Object.fromEntries([...entries].sort(([a], [b]) => a.localeCompare(b)))
232	}
233	
234	/**
235	 * Reads the repository branch and head for the manifest.
236	 * @returns {{ branch: string, head: string }}
237	 */
238	function readRepository() {
239	  const git = (args) => execFileSync('git', ['-C', REPO_DIR, ...args], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim()
240	  return { branch: git(['branch', '--show-current']), head: git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']) }
241	}
242	
243	/**
244	 * Reads every record and folds it into the dataset's files and manifest, writing nothing.
245	 * @param {{ name: string, includeDelegated: boolean, includeHeldOut: boolean }} options what to build
246	 * @returns {{ files: { path: string, content: string }[], manifest: object, hits: object[] }} the built dataset; a non-empty `hits` means it must not be written
247	 */
248	function buildDataset(options) {
249	  const catalog = readTaskCatalog()
250	  const counts = { seen: 0, train: 0, heldout: 0, withheldHeldOut: 0, delegated: 0, delegatedExcluded: 0, tamperedExcluded: 0, duplicatesDropped: 0 }
251	  const distributions = new Map()
252	  const tokens = newTokenTotals()
253	  const records = []
254	  const hits = []
255	  const seen = new Set()
256	  const trainLines = []
257	  const heldoutLines = []
258	
259	  for (const record of recordNames()) {
260	    const manifestPath = join(RUNS_DIR, record, 'manifest.json')
261	    if (!existsSync(manifestPath)) throw new Error(`${record} holds trajectories.jsonl but no manifest.json`)
262	    const manifestBytes = readFileSync(manifestPath)
263	    const recordManifest = JSON.parse(manifestBytes.toString('utf8'))
264	    records.push({
265	      record,
266	      composition: recordManifest.composition ?? null,
267	      head: recordManifest.repository?.head ?? null,
268	      manifestSha256: sha256(manifestBytes),
269	    })
270	
271	    const lines = readFileSync(join(RUNS_DIR, record, 'trajectories.jsonl'), 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean)
272	    // Sorting by id is stable, so duplicates inside one record stay in export order and the first one wins.
273	    const trajectories = lines.map(line => JSON.parse(line)).sort((a, b) => a.id.localeCompare(b.id))
274	    for (const trajectory of trajectories) {
275	      counts.seen += 1
276	      scanTrajectory(record, trajectory, hits)
277	      if (seen.has(trajectory.id)) { counts.duplicatesDropped += 1; continue }
278	      seen.add(trajectory.id)
279	      if (trajectory.reward.basis === 'tamper') { counts.tamperedExcluded += 1; continue }
280	
281	      const stamp = trajectory.environment
282	      const task = catalog.get(stamp?.environmentId)
283	      const delegated = (stamp?.implementer ?? 'route') !== 'route'
284	      if (delegated) counts.delegated += 1
285	      const dataset = {
286	        record,
287	        tier: task?.tier ?? null,
288	        domain: task?.domain ?? null,
289	        arm: armOf(stamp?.group),
290	        reward: { value: trajectory.reward.outcome, basis: trajectory.reward.basis },
291	      }
292	      const line = `${JSON.stringify({ ...trajectory, dataset })}\n`
293	
294	      if (stamp?.heldOut === true) {
295	        if (options.includeHeldOut) { heldoutLines.push(line); counts.heldout += 1 }
296	        else counts.withheldHeldOut += 1
297	        continue
298	      }
299	      if (delegated && !options.includeDelegated) { counts.delegatedExcluded += 1; continue }
300	
301	      trainLines.push(line)
302	      counts.train += 1
303	      addUsage(tokens, trajectory.steps)
304	      tally(distributions, 'arm', dataset.arm)
305	      tally(distributions, 'domain', dataset.domain ?? '(none)')
306	      tally(distributions, 'environment', stamp?.environmentId ?? '(none)')
307	      tally(distributions, 'implementer', stamp?.implementer ?? 'route')
308	      tally(distributions, 'ladder', stamp === undefined ? '(none)' : (stamp.ladder ?? [stamp.model]).map(routeOf).join('>'))
309	      tally(distributions, 'model', stamp === undefined ? '(none)' : routeOf(stamp.model))
310	      tally(distributions, 'reward', String(dataset.reward.value))
311	      tally(distributions, 'tier', dataset.tier === null ? '(none)' : String(dataset.tier))
312	    }
313	  }
314	
315	  if (tokens.stepsWithUsage === 0) tokens.note = 'no step of the written set reported usage'
316	  const files = [
317	    { path: 'train.jsonl', content: trainLines.join('') },
318	    { path: 'heldout.jsonl', content: heldoutLines.join('') },
319	  ]
320	  const manifest = {
321	    name: options.name,
322	    format: DATASET_FORMAT,
323	    builtAt: new Date().toISOString(),
324	    repository: readRepository(),
325	    tool: { path: TOOL_PATH, version: TOOL_VERSION },
326	    options: { includeDelegated: options.includeDelegated, includeHeldOut: options.includeHeldOut },
327	    records,
328	    counts,
329	    distributions: sorted([...distributions].map(([name, bucket]) => [name, sorted(bucket)])),
330	    tokens,
331	    files: files.map(({ path, content }) => ({ path, bytes: Buffer.byteLength(content, 'utf8'), sha256: sha256(content) })),
332	  }
333	  return { files, manifest, hits }
334	}
335	
336	/**
337	 * One line per count, per distribution, and per written file, for the console.
338	 * @param {object} manifest the manifest {@link buildDataset} produced
339	 * @returns {string} the summary, newline-joined
340	 */
341	function formatSummary(manifest) {
342	  const { counts, tokens } = manifest
343	  const lines = [
344	    `${manifest.name}: ${counts.train} train, ${counts.heldout} held out, of ${counts.seen} trajectories in ${manifest.records.length} records`,
345	    `  excluded: ${counts.withheldHeldOut} withheld held-out, ${counts.delegatedExcluded} delegated (${counts.delegated} seen), ${counts.tamperedExcluded} tampered, ${counts.duplicatesDropped} duplicates`,
346	    `  tokens: ${tokens.inputTokens} input, ${tokens.outputTokens} output, ${tokens.cacheReadTokens ?? 0} cache-read, ${tokens.cacheWriteTokens ?? 0} cache-write over ${tokens.stepsWithUsage} of ${tokens.steps} steps${tokens.note === undefined ? '' : ` (${tokens.note})`}`,
347	  ]
348	  for (const [name, bucket] of Object.entries(manifest.distributions)) {
349	    lines.push(`  ${name}: ${Object.entries(bucket).map(([key, count]) => `${key}=${count}`).join(' ')}`)
350	  }
351	  for (const file of manifest.files) lines.push(`  ${file.path}: ${file.bytes} bytes, ${file.sha256}`)
352	  return lines.join('\n')
353	}
354	
355	/**
356	 * Compares a rebuilt dataset with the manifest recorded beside it, and with
357	 * whichever of its files the repository carries.
358	 * @param {string} directory the dataset directory
359	 * @param {{ manifest: object }} built what {@link buildDataset} produced
360	 * @returns {string[]} one line per drift, empty when the recorded manifest matches
361	 */
362	function checkDataset(directory, built) {
363	  const manifestPath = join(directory, 'manifest.json')
364	  if (!existsSync(manifestPath)) return [`${relative(REPO_DIR, manifestPath)} does not exist; build the dataset first`]
365	  const recorded = JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifestPath, 'utf8'))
366	  const drift = []
367	  for (const file of built.manifest.files) {
368	    const entry = recorded.files.find(candidate => candidate.path === file.path)
369	    if (entry === undefined) { drift.push(`${file.path}: the recorded manifest lists no such file`); continue }
370	    if (entry.sha256 !== file.sha256) drift.push(`${file.path}: rebuilt ${file.sha256}, manifest records ${entry.sha256}`)
371	    if (entry.bytes !== file.bytes) drift.push(`${file.path}: rebuilt ${file.bytes} bytes, manifest records ${entry.bytes}`)
372	    const onDisk = join(directory, file.path)
373	    // A dataset too large to commit keeps only its manifest, so an absent file is not drift.
374	    if (existsSync(onDisk) && sha256(readFileSync(onDisk)) !== entry.sha256) drift.push(`${file.path}: the file in the repository does not match the manifest`)
375	  }
376	  for (const entry of recorded.files) {
377	    if (!built.manifest.files.some(file => file.path === entry.path)) drift.push(`${entry.path}: the rebuild writes no such file`)
378	  }
379	  if (JSON.stringify(recorded.counts) !== JSON.stringify(built.manifest.counts)) drift.push('counts: the rebuild does not reproduce the recorded counts')
380	  return drift
381	}
382	
383	function main() {
384	  const options = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))
385	  const directory = join(DATASETS_DIR, options.name)
386	  const built = buildDataset(options)
387	
388	  if (built.hits.length > 0) {
389	    console.error(`refusing to build ${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)}: ${built.hits.length} credential- or mailbox-shaped match(es); re-export the record, there is no accept flag`)
390	    for (const hit of built.hits) console.error(`  ${hit.record} ${hit.id} ${hit.path} ${hit.pattern} sha256=${hit.digest} ${hit.excerpt}`)
391	    process.exit(1)
392	  }
393	
394	  if (options.check) {
395	    const drift = checkDataset(directory, built)
396	    if (drift.length > 0) {
397	      console.error(`${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)} has drifted from its manifest:`)
398	      for (const line of drift) console.error(`  ${line}`)
399	      process.exit(1)
400	    }
401	    console.log(`${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)}: the rebuild matches the recorded manifest`)
402	    return
403	  }
404	
405	  mkdirSync(directory, { recursive: true })
406	  for (const file of built.files) writeFileSync(join(directory, file.path), file.content)
407	  writeFileSync(join(directory, 'manifest.json'), `${JSON.stringify(built.manifest, null, 2)}\n`)
408	  console.log(`wrote ${relative(REPO_DIR, directory)}`)
409	  console.log(formatSummary(built.manifest))
410	}
411	
412	main()
413

# The Proving Ground bench: thirty zero-dependency program tasks in three
# domains, registered from their task.json files, run on the operator's Claude
# Code subscription through the harness's own agent loop (the LLM route) or
# through the product's own loop (the external implementer), and compared in
# frozen paired experiments. No cadence: the drivers beside this file run one
# plan each.
#
# The route serves three product models under one provider. Every arm of an
# experiment names one of them, so a comparison between models and a comparison
# between implementers both read from the same catalog. The product envelope
# around each query is the one model-visible input the log does not hold.
- id: llm-claude-code
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-claude-code'
  config:
    provider: claude-code
    models:
      - id: opus
        name: Claude Code opus
        productModel: opus
        contextWindow: 200000
      - id: sonnet
        name: Claude Code sonnet
        productModel: sonnet
        contextWindow: 200000
      - id: haiku
        name: Claude Code haiku
        productModel: haiku
        contextWindow: 200000
    effort: medium
    queryTimeoutMs: 300000

# Managed child-process groups for the bash executor, for the CLI the route
# spawns per query, and for the product the external implementer spawns.
- id: subprocess
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess-local'

- id: sandbox
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-local'

# workspace-write over the cell session's own cwd, which the runner sets to the
# cell workspace. The configured root is the fallback for the agentless calls
# the runner itself makes: the checks run outside every session, so they still
# read the reservation the cells are denied.
- id: sandbox-policy
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-sandbox-policy'
  config:
    mode: workspace-write
    workspaceRoot: !!js process.cwd()

- id: bash

./.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-05-environment-runner.md:29:**Report and record.** `run()` returns the environment id, the session id, the stamp exactly as appended, one entry per attempt with its check results and workspace digest, whether the run certified, the certificate when it did, and the accumulated model usage, after flushing the session. The durable record is the session log itself: the stamp, `goal/change`, the five `verification/*` events including one `verification/run` per attempt — its results whether they passed or failed, its attempt number within the standard, the executor, and the workspace digest the checks read — and the messages. Token ids and logprobs are absent by design: the harness never sees token ids, and on-policy capture belongs to a trainer's inference proxy, as Agent Lightning and Polar do it. [`dsh-data-use`](../../../../packages/governance/data-use/README.md) pins the terms at session creation and its README says outright that nothing enforces them; the [attributable-decisions note](2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md) defers that enforcement to its rollout item 2. Redaction therefore fails safe: a field added to the record type is redacted until someone decides otherwise, rather than exported until someone notices.
./.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-06-curator.zh.md:11:这两项承诺都没有产出方。[`dsh-trajectories`](../../../../packages/improvement/trajectories/README.md) 直接从折叠写出 `dsh-trajectory/1` 行：它按 `environment/run` stamp 扣留留出会话与区会话并对每一条被扣留者计数，却不做任何脱敏、不读取 `dataUse/terms`、也不留下 manifest，因此它自己的 README 把"无脱敏"列为限制并指向遥测规则作为先例。[`dsh-data-use`](../../../../packages/governance/data-use/README.md) 在会话创建时钉定条款，其 README 直言没有任何东西执行它们；[可归属决定笔记](2026-09-06-attributable-decisions.md)把这项执行推迟给它的推进项 2。与此同时，[竞品基线笔记](2026-09-06-competitive-baselines.md)记录了 Village 数据集的研究许可证在没有书面许可时禁止训练，并断定在扣留可被证明之前没有任何流水线可以摄入它。今天，一次 `ctx.trajectories.export()` 调用就会把一份客户转录、其中的凭据与其仅供评估的样本写进同一个训练文件，而仓库里没有任何东西说这是错的。

23:The record format is `dsh-trajectory/1`: one JSON object per line whose `messages` follow the chat-completion message list every trainer's chat template consumes, with rewards and provenance beside them. Token ids and logprobs are absent by design: the harness never sees token ids, and on-policy capture belongs to a trainer's inference proxy, as Agent Lightning and Polar do it. Prior art for the shape: verifiers' `Trace` (a message graph with tool calls, driven through an OpenAI-dialect interception server), SWE-agent and SWE-smith trajectory files, and the OpenAI chat-completion message list.
59:Off-policy text. A trainer re-tokenizes exported text through its chat template, which suits supervised and rejection-sampled training and not strict on-policy reinforcement learning; the record format states this, and on-policy runs go through an inference proxy in front of the same harness.

# Environments and trajectories

English | [中文](improvement.zh.md)

1	# AGENTS.md — The documentation standard
2	
3	This file defines document structure, Markdown tiers, writing rules, and `verify-doc-budgets` ceilings. Use [dsh-doc-standards](../.agents/skills/dsh-doc-standards/SKILL.md) for placement and validation, and [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for required coverage and editorial judgment; the [doc-tiers Agent Note](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-04-doc-tiers-and-budgets.md) owns rationale.
4	
5	## Document structure
6	
7	These rules apply to human-facing documentation; [Agent Notes](../.agents/notes/README.md) remain outside their scope. A [postmortem](postmortem/README.md) is an incident-scoped reference; chronology records evidence, not a teaching sequence. A document's subject and tree position fix its scope: describe its own subject at appropriate detail and direct children only by purpose, responsibility, and high-level behavior; link to the owning descendant for lower-level detail. Document type does not widen that scope. A reference may be exhaustive only about its own subject. Testing mechanisms, fixtures, and harnesses belong at the lowest owning level; higher documents link there.
8	
9	Classify every in-scope document as a tutorial or reference. Tutorials follow an ordered path to an outcome and introduce only what each step needs. References define a lookup scope and current behavior without a teaching sequence. Separate substantial tutorial and reference content; label a section when either part is small.
10	
11	Before writing a tutorial, privately classify the reader's starting knowledge and each concept as beginner, intermediate, or advanced. Establish prerequisites before dependent concepts, increase difficulty gradually, and move unnecessary advanced material to a later tutorial or reference.
12	
13	Author in this order: locate the document in the tree; set its permitted detail; choose tutorial or reference; for a tutorial, order concepts by prerequisite and difficulty; relocate descendant-owned detail; replace lower-level explanations with links to their owners.
14	
15	## The tier taxonomy: one home per fact
16	
17	Each fact has one home: the tier whose job it is; elsewhere, link there.
18	
19	| Tier | Job | Does NOT belong there |
20	|---|---|---|
21	| Root `AGENTS.md` | Standing orders: rules an agent needs in context in every session, one to three lines each, linking its home | Stories, worked examples, situational procedures, anything restated from a linked home |
22	| Subtree `AGENTS.md` (`packages/`, `examples/`, `docs/`, `.agents/notes/`) | Orders specific to that subtree | Repo-wide rules the root file already carries |
23	| [architecture.md](architecture.md) | Ordered map: composition, core packages, loop, seams, extension points; read before changing `packages/` | Type definitions (→ subsystems), per-package detail (→ package READMEs), decision rationale (→ Agent Notes), implementation-status annotations |
24	| [subsystems/](subsystems/README.md) | One reference page per subsystem: type definitions, semantics, and the generated Cordis API | Behavior narration (→ architecture.md) |
25	| [Agent Notes](../.agents/notes/README.md) | Active decision records: the why, what-was-given-up, and required verification; `implemented/` notes describe shipped reality in present tense | Migration plans, acceptance-task checklists, fixture walkthroughs, and spec-speak ("should…") once the decision has shipped; archived notes are frozen history, never current authority |
26	| [postmortem/](postmortem/README.md) | Incident stories — the only tier where war-story narrative belongs | — |
27	| [cookbook/](cookbook/adding-a-package.md) | Step-by-step how-tos with numbered verify steps | Design rationale (→ the Agent Note each guide links) |
28	| [user/](user/index.md) | Product-facing guides published by the documentation website | Generated reference tables, contributor procedures, decision history |
29	| Package README | The per-package contract: config, semantics, limitations, extension points, and [Model Experience](cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme) | JSDoc restatement, generated-catalog restatement (event/tool tables), other packages' concerns |
30	| [development.md](development.md) | Contributor setup, daily workflow, and a summary of CI; a bilingual pair under the [i18n contract](i18n/README.md) | Runtime/version rationale (→ Agent Notes), check-by-check lists that drift from `package.json` scripts |
31	| Generated reference: the per-page `cordis-surface` regions in [subsystems/](subsystems/README.md), the [Cordis core API + inherited tier](cordis-api/context.md), [tool-catalog](tool-catalog.md), [config-catalog](config-catalog.md), [persistence-catalog](persistence-catalog.md), [module-graph.md](module-graph.md) | Exhaustive English sources regenerated from source and freshness-gated; reviewed Chinese counterparts follow the [pairing workflow](i18n/README.md#scope-and-exclusions) | Hand edits to generated English sources or regions; Chinese counterparts update through pairing only |
32	| Skills (`.agents/skills/`) | Reusable workflows and specialized decision standards | Product and runtime contracts (→ docs or source) |
33	
34	Placement: bugs → postmortems; rationale → Agent Notes; procedures → cookbooks; type definitions → subsystems; package contracts → READMEs; standing orders → root `AGENTS.md` with a rationale link.
35	
36	## Writing rules
37	
38	- **Document current state, not change history.** Avoid "previously/now/no longer", PRs, commits, and stack positions in durable prose; name the live mechanism. Put change stories in commits, PRs, Agent Notes, or postmortems; the latter two may cite merged PRs and issues as evidence.
39	- **Every non-trivial change includes at least one Agent Note in the same PR.** Update the owning note or add one; only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](../.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)).
40	- **One physical line per paragraph** (`verify-md-wrap`): use editor soft-wrap. Code blocks, tables, and list structure keep their formatting; code comments stay under the linter's column limit.
41	- **Fenced `ts` blocks must compile** (`doc-typecheck`); a pasted type declaration and its original JSDoc use ` ```ts type-equiv `, while a body-stripped public class declaration uses ` ```ts public-api `; register either in the manifest so neither can drift ([mechanics](development.md#documenting-types-verbatim-ts-type-equiv)).
42	- **The owning [subsystems page](subsystems/README.md) updates in the same change** that reshapes a documented type. `verify-type-equiv` catches drifted pastes, not never-documented new types; a type is documented on its declaring package group's page ([page scoping](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-03-package-anchored-subsystem-pages.md)).
43	- **Pairs update together**: [Terminology-guided](i18n/terminology.md), single-pass active-agent work repositions first-use annotations, preserves untouched prose, and re-records; `dsh-translate-docs` remains user-invoked ([contract](i18n/README.md)).
44	- **Comments and JSDoc state complete contracts, not reasoning transcripts.** Preserve behavior, failure, timing, ownership, modality, exceptions, consequences, and non-obvious orientation; delete narration, test walkthroughs, review analysis, and code restatement. Keep the local contract and link its rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for details.
45	- Write directly: name actors and facts ([decision](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-09-concrete-prose-names-actors-and-recorded-facts.md)). Reserve `seam` for the defined capability. Name the exact check, type, API, operation, or behavior instead of metaphorical "gate", "vocabulary", or "surface".
46	
47	## Wordcount Budgets
48	
49	[scripts/doc-budgets.manifest.json](../scripts/doc-budgets.manifest.json) sets standing-doc ceilings; `pnpm run verify-doc-budgets` rejects excess or missing files.
50	
51	When the gate goes red:
52	
53	1. **Relocate** content that belongs in another tier; leave a one-line link if needed.
54	2. **Condense** content that belongs here but can be shorter.
55	3. **Raise** the ceiling only when the words need the space; justify the manifest diff in the PR. A too-low ceiling is a budget bug.
56	
57	Ceilings are guardrails, not reduction targets. At or below target, retain at least 5% headroom; above target, freeze the ceiling until relocation or condensation brings the document under target. Lower a ceiling only when the document still has room, and raise it when content would otherwise be deleted. Targets: root `AGENTS.md` ≤ 1,600 words; `architecture.md` ≤ 1,800; subtree `AGENTS.md` ≤ 600, except `packages/AGENTS.md` ≤ 650 and this file ≤ 1,250; `packages/README.md` ≤ 600. Review governs unbudgeted tiers.
58	
59	## The slop checklist
60	
61	Hunt these in any doc; [dsh-doc-standards](../.agents/skills/dsh-doc-standards/SKILL.md) runs this list as an audit:
62	
63	- The same rule stated in more than one home. Grep a distinctive phrase; keep one home and link the rest.
64	- Narrated history or war stories: "previously", "now", "no longer", "used to", "renamed", "was moved", PRs, or commits. State the current fact; link an Agent Note or postmortem when needed.
65	- Implementation-status annotations in prose or diagrams ("implemented!", "future: …"). Status rots; the repo layout and package manifests carry it.
66	- Hand-restated catalogs, JSDoc, or inventories of tests, packages, and status when source or a generator is authoritative.
67	- Reasoning transcripts: step-by-step implementation narration, proof of obvious branches, test walkthroughs, or rejected local alternatives. Keep the resulting contract or durable rationale; delete the path used to derive it.
68	- Rationale repeated beside sibling methods instead of once at the owning capability or helper.
69	- Paragraph walls: one paragraph carrying several rules and parenthetical asides. Split it or demote the detail to its home.
70	- Emphasis inflation: bold, CAPS, or "critically" everywhere means nothing stands out. Reserve emphasis for the clause that changes behavior.
71	- Spec-speak in `implemented/` Agent Notes: "should", migration plans, acceptance checklists. An implemented Agent Note describes what is, per the [implemented-note instructions](../.agents/notes/implemented/AGENTS.md).
72	
73	## Cross-reference with machine-checkable links, never free prose
74	
75	Link repository references with relative Markdown paths, never bare filenames or Agent Note numbers. `verify-md-links` rejects missing targets and dead `#fragment` anchors ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-06-18-markdown-cross-link-lint.md)).
76

content.content: 211:## Trajectory reward 212- 213-The reward carries its basis: `tamper` when the last recorded run found the check-owned files changed (`0`, whatever else the log holds), `certificate` when a completion standard existed for the goal (the verifier decided, `1` with a covering certificate and `0` without), `uncertified-completion` when the goal completed with no standard ever authored, and `none` when the log holds no goal. 214- 215-```ts type-equiv 216-/** The reward with its basis and the evidence behind it. */ 217-interface TrajectoryReward { 218- /** `1` for a certified completion, `0` for a measured goal without a covering certificate, `null` when no verifier decided. */ 219- readonly outcome: 1 | 0 | null 220- readonly basis: TrajectoryRewardBasis 221- /** Goal the reward measures, absent when the log holds none. */ 222- readonly goal?: TrajectoryGoal 223- /** Certificate covering the current standard revision, present only when `outcome` is `1`. */ 224- readonly certificate?: VerificationCertificate 225- /** Directives the validator issued during the session. */ 226- readonly directives: number 227- /** Checks relaxed out of the standard during the session. */ 228- readonly relaxations: number 229- /** Runs of the standard recorded during the session, passing or failing. */ 230- readonly attempts: number 231-} 232-``` 233- 234-The record carries `parity` beside `reward`: the `{ weightPassed, weightTotal }` of the last recorded run, absent when that run measured no cases. It is an auxiliary signal a shaped reward may read and never a replacement for the certificate-based `outcome`, which a weighted pass rate cannot decide. 235- 236-Messages are projected from the session surface after compaction replacements, each carrying the seq of its source event; token ids and logprobs are absent because the harness never sees them. 237- 238-## Session facts 239- 240-The scorekeeper folds one session log into four groups, served both as the `sessionFacts` projection value of a live session and as the record `ctx.scorekeeper.facts()` reads out of persistence. Every field folds from a named session event; the source event of each one is tabulated in [the package README](../../packages/improvement/scorekeeper/README.md). Cost is one of them: the efficiency group sums the `costEur` the `usage/priced` records themselves state and keeps their `pricingDigests`, taking no pricing table of its own, and withholds the sum entirely when a usage-bearing step went unpriced. A scoreboard row is these records grouped by model route, environment, isolation level, implementer, held-out split, and district, and it carries a cost per certified session only when every certified session of the row states one. The outcome group carries the last run's `parity` beside `certified`, and a row means it over the sessions that measured cases: the certificate and the weighted pass rate are separate columns, never merged into one score and never ranked across. Two facts a publication reads sit beside them: `tamper` is the last run's verdict, `not-instrumented` for a session that recorded none, and the identity group's `compositionSha256` is the digest of the last `composition/manifest` in the log; a row states the digest only when every session of it states the same one, counts its `tampered` sessions and the reads the barrier refused across them, and lists the distinct executors of its certificates. 241- 242-```ts type-equiv 243-/** One session log folded into the four fact groups. */ 244-interface SessionFacts { 245- readonly identity: SessionFactsIdentity 246- readonly outcome: SessionFactsOutcome 247- readonly efficiency: SessionFactsEfficiency 248- readonly tools: SessionFactsTools 249-} 250-``` 251- -- 912:Trajectory exporter (`ctx.trajectories`): persisted sessions as training and evaluation records. 913- 914-```ts cordis-catalog 915-/** 916- * Fold the requested sessions and write one line per trajectory. A session 917- * that cannot be read or folded is reported and the export continues; the 918- * sink is closed exactly once when every session has been handled. 919- * @param request - sessions to export, the destination sink, the reward filter, the held-out opt-in, and the districts to write. 920- * @returns counts of sessions, written lines, rewarded lines, filtered 921- * sessions, withheld held-out and district sessions, and skips with reasons. 922- */ 923-async export(request: TrajectoryExportRequest): Promise 924-``` 925- 926-Source: [`packages/improvement/trajectories/src/index.ts:80`](../../packages/improvement/trajectories/src/index.ts) 927- 928- 929- 930-### `fleet/*` events 931- 932- 933- 934-#### `fleet/cell` — emit 935- 936-One cell of a running plan settled: the fleet has recorded its outcome and applied the configured workspace retention. Observe-only — a listener cannot change the outcome, and its failure is contained without failing the cell. Cells are emitted in settle order, which equals plan order only while `maxConcurrent` is `1`. 937- 938-```ts cordis-catalog 939-/** 940- * One cell of a running plan settled: the fleet has recorded its outcome 941- * and applied the configured workspace retention. Observe-only — a 942- * listener cannot change the outcome, and its failure is contained without 943- * failing the cell. Cells are emitted in settle order, which equals plan 944- * order only while `maxConcurrent` is `1`. 945- * @param payload.group - batch identity every run stamp of this fleet run carries. 946- * @param payload.district - district the plan stamped its cells with, absent for a plan outside every district. 947- * @param payload.cell - the environment, model route, and repetition that settled. 948- * @param payload.outcome - the session and certification of a reported cell, or the code and message of a cell that produced none. 949- * @mode emit 950- */ 951-'fleet/cell'(payload: FleetCellEvent): void 952-```

151	
152	/**
153	 * Compile one configured profile, refusing every rule a load may not accept.
154	 * @param id - the profile id, named in every rejection.
155	 * @param config - the profile's shipped-rule choice and its own rules.
156	 * @returns the compiled profile with its digest.
157	 * @throws {@link CuratorError} `CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG` when the profile holds
158	 *   no rule, or when a rule has an empty id, an id another rule in the same
159	 *   profile already used, the sticky flag, or a pattern that does not compile.
160	 */
161	export function compileProfile(id: string, config: RedactionProfileConfig): RedactionProfile {
162	  const rules = [...config.shipped ? SHIPPED_REDACTION_RULES : [], ...config.rules ?? []]
163	  if (rules.length === 0) {
164	    throw new CuratorError(
165	      `redaction profile "${id}" lists no rule and does not take the shipped set, so it would redact nothing`,
166	      'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG',
167	    )
168	  }
169	  const seen = new Set<string>()
170	  const compiled = rules.map((rule) => {
171	    if (rule.id.length === 0) throw new CuratorError(`redaction profile "${id}" has a rule with an empty id`, 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
172	    if (seen.has(rule.id)) {
173	      throw new CuratorError(`redaction profile "${id}" lists rule "${rule.id}" twice, so its hit count would name two rules`, 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
174	    }
175	    seen.add(rule.id)
176	    return { id: rule.id, regex: compileRule(id, rule), replacement: rule.replacement }
177	  })
178	  return { id, rules: compiled, sha256: profileDigest(compiled) }
179	}
180	
181	/**
182	 * Compile one rule's pattern, always globally.
183	 * @param profileId - owning profile, named in a rejection.
184	 * @param rule - the configured rule.
185	 * @returns the compiled expression.
186	 * @throws {@link CuratorError} on the sticky flag or an uncompilable pattern.
187	 */
188	function compileRule(profileId: string, rule: RedactionRule): RegExp {
189	  const flags = rule.flags ?? ''
190	  if (flags.includes('y')) {
191	    throw new CuratorError(
192	      `redaction rule "${rule.id}" of profile "${profileId}" sets the sticky flag, which would match only at the expression's last index and leave later hits in the record`,
193	      'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG',
194	    )
195	  }
196	  try {
197	    return new RegExp(rule.pattern, flags.includes('g') ? flags : `${flags}g`)
198	  } catch (error: unknown) {
199	    // The RegExp constructor is the only thrower here and it throws a SyntaxError.
200	    throw new CuratorError(`redaction rule "${rule.id}" of profile "${profileId}" does not compile: ${String(error)}`, 'CURATOR_INVALID_CONFIG')
201	  }
202	}
203	
204	/**
205	 * Digest the rules that will actually run, so a manifest states which rules a
206	 * profile name stood for rather than only the name.
207	 * @param rules - the compiled rules in run order.
208	 * @returns lowercase SHA-256 hex over their canonical encoding.
209	 */
210	function profileDigest(rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[]): string {
211	  const canonical = rules.map(rule => ({
212	    id: rule.id,
213	    source: rule.regex.source,
214	    flags: rule.regex.flags,
215	    replacement: rule.replacement,
216	  }))
217	  return createHash('sha256').update(JSON.stringify(canonical)).digest('hex')
218	}
219	
220	/**
221	 * Replace every match of every rule, in rule order, counting the replacements.
222	 * The replacement is returned from a function, so a `$&` or `$1` a deployment
223	 * configured is written literally and can never splice the matched text back in.
224	 * @param text - the string to redact.
225	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
226	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
227	 * @returns the redacted string.
228	 */
229	export function applyRules(text: string, rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[], hits: Map<string, number>): string {
230	  let redacted = text
231	  for (const rule of rules) {
232	    redacted = redacted.replace(rule.regex, () => {
233	      hits.set(rule.id, (hits.get(rule.id) ?? 0) + 1)
234	      return rule.replacement
235	    })
236	  }
237	  return redacted
238	}
239	
240	/**
241	 * Whether one string keeps its exact value.
242	 * @param site - where the string sits in the record.
243	 * @returns true for the record's identifiers, discriminants, and tool names.
244	 */
245	function keeps(site: RedactionSite): boolean {
246	  return NEVER_REDACTED_SUBTREES.has(site.root)
247	    || NEVER_REDACTED_KEYS.has(site.key)
248	    || NEVER_REDACTED_PATHS.has(site.path)
249	}
250	
251	/**
252	 * Redact one value and everything under it.
253	 * @param value - the value at `site`.
254	 * @param site - where the value sits in the record.
255	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
256	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
257	 * @returns the value with every redacted string replaced.
258	 */
259	function redactValue(value: unknown, site: RedactionSite, rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[], hits: Map<string, number>): unknown {
260	  if (typeof value === 'string') return keeps(site) ? value : applyRules(value, rules, hits)
261	  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(item => redactValue(item, site, rules, hits))
262	  if (typeof value === 'object' && value !== null) return redactEntries(value, site, rules, hits)
263	  return value
264	}
265	
266	/**
267	 * Redact every property of one object, descending with the property's path.
268	 * @param value - the object to walk.
269	 * @param site - where the object sits, or `undefined` at the record root.
270	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
271	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
272	 * @returns a new object with the same keys.
273	 */
274	function redactEntries(
275	  value: object,
276	  site: RedactionSite | undefined,
277	  rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[],
278	  hits: Map<string, number>,
279	): Record<string, unknown> {
280	  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(value).map(([key, entry]) => [
281	    key,
282	    redactValue(entry, site === undefined ? { root: key, path: key, key } : { root: site.root, path: `${site.path}.${key}`, key }, rules, hits),
283	  ]))
284	}
285	
286	/**
287	 * Apply a profile to one trajectory record. Every string is redacted except the
288	 * record's identifiers, its readers' discriminants, and registered tool names,
289	 * so a field added to the record format is redacted until someone decides
290	 * otherwise rather than exported until someone notices.
291	 * @param record - the folded record, as the exporter serialized it.
292	 * @param rules - the profile's rules in run order.
293	 * @param hits - replacement counts per rule id, incremented in place.
294	 * @returns a new record with the same keys and every redacted string replaced.
295	 */
296	export function redactTrajectory(record: Trajectory, rules: readonly CompiledRedactionRule[], hits: Map<string, number>): Trajectory {
297	  // The walk replaces string leaves and preserves every key, so the result is
298	  // the same record format with redacted text.
299	  return redactEntries(record, undefined, rules, hits) as unknown as Trajectory
300	}
